set_note: 1.1 published 2026-09-25; 1.2 (2026-09-28, additive) adds the REPLY_ prefix and six exact REPLY_ codes for synchronous reply mode (W2-8, envelope README 2.3.2 and 2.3.3, channel-spec README 3.2.6). 1.3 (2026-09-29, additive) registers the fixed names the wave 2 loaders emit under reserved prefixes, several of which were already named in channel-spec README 3.4 but never registered (rule 2), plus TLS_PEER_NOT_ALLOWED for the receivers' mTLS allow-list (channel-spec README 3.2.7). No prefix added. 1.4 (2026-09-29, additive) registers REPLY_EXPIRED, the worker's code for a reply skipped past its deadline, carried on a replied event with status dropped (envelope README 2.3.2). 1.7 (2026-10-05, additive) registers REPLY_BODY_INVALID and REPLY_BODY_OVER_BUDGET, the receivers' codes for a body: step reply body they cannot write (channel-spec README 3.2.6, set 1.7 receiver rules). Sets 1.5 and 1.6 did not change this file.
note: Rationale and rules: envelope/v0 README 2.3.2. The contract is the source; tributary.sdk.codes is checked against this file by a tributary-sdk test (ENGINE_CODES == codes + log_only; RESERVED_PREFIXES == reserved_prefixes). A channel's Reject(code) may not use any code listed here or any code under a reserved prefix. Codes only, never values: this file is PHI-free by construction.

reserved_prefixes.owner: http and fhir loaders: HTTP_<status>, HTTP_REDIRECT_REFUSED (channel-spec README 3.4)
fhir loader: FHIR_BUNDLE_INVALID, FHIR_ENTRY_FAILED, FHIR_RESPONSE_INVALID (channel-spec README 3.4.2). No run-time-minted members
sftp loader and source: SFTP_<numeric status>, plus SFTP_NAME_CONFLICT (channel-spec README 3.4)
sftp loader and source: SSH_HOST_KEY_MISMATCH, SSH_AUTH_FAILED (channel-spec README 3.4)
s3 loader: S3_<ERROR_CODE> minted from the store's code, plus the fixed names in codes. A minted code equal to a fixed name is emitted as S3_UNKNOWN (channel-spec README 3.4, set 1.3)
mllp loader: MLLP_AE, MLLP_AR, MLLP_TIMEOUT, MLLP_NO_ACK (channel-spec README 3.4.6)
kafka loader: KAFKA_<librdkafka error name> (channel-spec README 3.4.7)
synchronous reply path, receivers and pipeline worker (channel-spec README 3.2.6). Set 1.2

codes.emitter: runtime executor, wave 1 to W2-5 builds only
codes.meaning: Pre-fix spelling of TRANSFORM_ERROR (envelope 2.3.2). Not emitted once the executor is corrected
A record the pipeline built fails the envelope at produce time (size, header count or a header rule). The CONSUMED record is dead-lettered with its raw payload; nothing is produced for it
One consumed record outlasted its processing budget, sized under max.poll.interval.ms. The consumed record is dead-lettered instead of evicting the consumer in a loop

A dead letter cannot be written because the record breaks the envelope even when reduced (e.g. a raw payload over the 1,000,000-byte inline limit). Carried by a partition_halted EVENT, never on a record: the loop halts the partition, commits nothing and loses nothing. Same outcome as channel-spec D16 for a Kafka source that cannot dead-letter
The executor returned neither a message nor a drop
Local producer queue full; back-pressure
The Kafka client refused the produce call
Records still queued when the flush deadline passed
A delivery callback reported failure
A Kafka transaction was aborted
The destination circuit breaker is open
Could not connect to the destination (channel-spec README 3.4)
Peer certificate verification failed (channel-spec README 3.4)
Transport failure after connecting
timeoutMs elapsed (channel-spec README 3.4)
Payload is not the shape the destination type requires (channel-spec README 3.4.3)
onUnresolved: reject and the field did not resolve (channel-spec README 3.3.2)
Not HL7 v2 ER7, claim-checked, or no leading MSH (channel-spec README 3.3.2)
A segment in requireSegments does not occur (channel-spec README 3.3.2)
MSH-12.1 absent or not listed in version (channel-spec README 3.3.2)
More than 10,000 children (channel-spec README 3.3.2 split rule 4)
Input the splitter cannot read (channel-spec README 3.3.2)

codes.emitter: mllp and http receivers, sync mode (sender-facing MSA-3 and metrics; never a header or event)
codes.meaning: Committed; no reply before reply.timeoutMs after the raw commit callback. MLLP AE (channel-spec README 3.2.6)

codes.emitter: mllp and http receivers, sync mode (sender-facing; never a header or event)
codes.meaning: Committed; the reply partition this request advertised was revoked, so its reply is unreachable. Answered only after the raw commit callback succeeded. MLLP AE

codes.emitter: mllp and http receivers, sync mode (sender-facing; never a header or event)
codes.meaning: Not published: the pending map is at reply.maxPending. MLLP AR

codes.emitter: mllp and http receivers, sync mode (sender-facing; never a header or event)
codes.meaning: Not published: this process holds no reply partition or its reply consumer is not connected. MLLP AR; the process also fails readiness

body: step and no pipeline step called ctx.reply on a message that was not dropped. The reply is failed (tb-error-code on the reply record, and the replied event); the message was routed, so there is no dlq record

codes.emitter: mllp receiver, sync mode, body: step (sender-facing MSA-3 and metrics; never a header or event)
codes.meaning: Set 1.7. Committed and routed; the step's reply body contains an MLLP framing byte (0x0B or 0x1C), so it is not written. The reply is treated as failed: MLLP AE. Not REPLY_BODY_MISSING, which is the worker's no-ctx.reply code (channel-spec README 3.2.6)

codes.emitter: mllp and http receivers, sync mode, body: step (sender-facing MSA-3 and metrics; never a header or event)
codes.meaning: Set 1.7. Committed and routed; the step's reply body cannot be charged to queue.maxBytes when it arrives, so it is not held. The reply is treated as failed: MLLP AE. Not REPLY_BUSY, which means not published (AR) (channel-spec README 3.2.6)

codes.emitter: runtime worker, sync mode (replied EVENT only, status dropped; never a header, never sender-facing)
codes.meaning: Set 1.4. The raw record's tb-reply-deadline plus the 5 s skew allowance had passed when the worker finished it, so no reply was produced. The message itself was processed normally. The sender already got AE / REPLY_TIMEOUT from its receiver; this code explains that answer in the archive and the browser (channel-spec README 3.2.6)

tb-reply-partition malformed or out of range, or tb-reply-deadline malformed, on a raw record. The message is processed normally and no reply is produced; carried by a replied EVENT only (envelope README 2.3.3). Named REPLY_PARTITION_INVALID in the W2-8 proposal; renamed to cover both headers
A 3xx response. Redirects are never followed (channel-spec README 3.4 rule 1). Not retryable. Set 1.3: named in README 3.4 since set 1.1, registered now

Payload is not a transaction Bundle, or has an entry that is not idempotent by construction; checked before sending. Not retryable (channel-spec README 3.4.2). Set 1.3: named since set 1.1, registered now
2xx transaction-response in which an entry status is >= 400. Retryable only if a failed entry is 408, 409, 429 or 5xx (channel-spec README 3.4.2). Set 1.3
2xx without a parseable transaction-response of the request's entry count (a gateway page, a truncated or oversize body). Retryable: every entry is idempotent (channel-spec README 3.4.2). Set 1.3
Error response carrying no ClickHouse exception code (for example a proxy's error page). Not retryable (channel-spec README 3.4). Set 1.3
The deterministic remote name exists with a different size: it is not this message. Not retryable, never a silent success (channel-spec README 3.4, 3.4.4). Set 1.3
Server host key not among the pinned fingerprints. Not retryable (channel-spec README 3.4). Set 1.3: named since set 1.1, registered now
Server refused the credentials. Not retryable (channel-spec README 3.4). Set 1.3: named since set 1.1, registered now
The deterministic key exists with a different size: it is not this message. Not retryable, never a silent success (channel-spec README 3.4, 3.4.5). Set 1.3
A conditional put answered 412 and the object was gone by the HEAD. Retryable. Set 1.3
No credentials found for auth ambient. Not retryable. Set 1.3
The store's error code is absent or not a plain token, or it would map onto another registered fixed S3_ name (channel-spec README 3.4). Set 1.3
Downstream answered AE (channel-spec README 3.4.6). Set 1.3: named since set 1.1, registered now
Downstream answered AR (channel-spec README 3.4.6). Set 1.3: named since set 1.1, registered now
No ACK within timeoutMs (channel-spec README 3.4.6). Set 1.3: named since set 1.1, registered now

Connection closed before a complete ACK, an unparseable ACK, an ACK for another control id, or an MSA-1 outside HL7's enumeration. Retryable (channel-spec README 3.4.6). Set 1.3: named since set 1.1, registered now

codes.emitter: mllp and http receivers (log line and metrics only; never a header or event)
codes.meaning: The client certificate chained but carries no subjectAltName listed in tls.allowedClientSans; the connection is refused before any application byte is read (channel-spec README 3.2.7). Set 1.3
